standard.title: Locate and process information in texts
standard.description: locate and process information and ideas in familiar spoken, written and multimodal texts, responding in ways appropriate to cultural context, purpose and audience
standard.prior_knowledge: Students enter the Y7-10 sequence without prior formal target language study. They bring general literacy strategies from English and may have incidental exposure to the target language. They have not yet applied information-locating strategies to target language texts across spoken, written and multimodal modes.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students locate and process specific information and ideas from familiar spoken, written and multimodal texts in the target language, and respond in ways that demonstrate awareness of cultural context, purpose and intended audience.

nodes.label: Identifying key information in familiar texts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify specific details and key points of information in familiar spoken, written or multimodal texts in the target language.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least three specific pieces of information from one familiar text type (e.g. a menu, timetable, short announcement or simple written notice) in the target language.
nodes.typical_width: Locate and classify key information from a range of familiar text types (menus, notices, timetables, packaging, schedules); use comprehension strategies (skimming, scanning, using contextual cues) to locate specific details.
wider: Compare information located in equivalent text types from the target language community and Australia — identify differences in how information is structured or presented
Navigate an authentic digital resource (map, timetable, website) from a target language community to locate specific information for a real purpose
nodes.hinge_reason: Locating specific information is the prerequisite for all processing and responding tasks in EC04. Students who rely only on global comprehension (understanding 'roughly what it is about') cannot satisfy the descriptor's demand to locate and process specific ideas. EC05's translation and interpretation tasks also depend on this capacity.

response_modes.reason: Students need explicit instruction in comprehension strategies (scanning for key words, using layout and headings, making predictions from context) before they can apply them independently to target language texts. Modelling the strategy process — not just assigning texts — is the lever.
Exposing students to a range of familiar text types ensures comprehension strategies are not locked to one text format. Scanning a menu requires different cues than scanning a timetable.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Authentic text types from target language communities provide early, meaningful intercultural contact — students encounter how information is structured differently across cultural contexts, not just language differences.
success_criteria: Can locate at least three specific pieces of information from a familiar target language text using comprehension strategies
Can identify the purpose and intended audience of a familiar text type in the target language

nodes.label: Processing information across text types
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can process information from spoken, written and multimodal texts in the target language, summarising or classifying key ideas.
nodes.minimum_width: Process information from at least one spoken or multimodal text (not only written) — e.g. identify key points from a short recording or video.
nodes.typical_width: Locate and process information from spoken, written and multimodal texts; summarise, classify or compare information across sources; conduct and report simple information-gathering tasks such as surveys or brief interviews.
wider: Compare information across two or more sources on the same topic — identify where sources agree or differ
Locate and process information from a First Nations Australian context presented in or translated into the target language — reflect on what is gained or lost in the shift

response_modes.reason: Processing spoken texts requires different strategies from written text processing — prosody, pace and speaker variation all carry meaning. Ensuring students process across modalities prevents over-reliance on written text as the primary comprehension mode.

success_criteria: Can identify and summarise key points from a short spoken or multimodal text in the target language
Can compare or classify information from at least two texts on the same topic

nodes.label: Responding appropriately to cultural context
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can respond to texts in ways that demonstrate awareness of the cultural context, purpose and audience of the original text.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce one response to a target language text that demonstrates awareness of at least one contextual factor (e.g. the text's purpose, its intended audience, or a cultural reference within it).
nodes.typical_width: Respond to a range of target language texts by identifying cultural references, intended purpose and audience; produce responses (written, spoken or multimodal) that are appropriate to the context and audience of the original text.
wider: Respond to imaginative texts (story, comic, film clip) from the target language community by identifying and discussing cultural assumptions or values embedded in the text
Compare responses to the same text produced by a target language community member and an Australian English speaker — identify where cultural context shapes interpretation differently

response_modes.reason: Cultural context awareness requires students to move beyond 'what does it say' to 'why does it say it this way, and for whom'. Explicit discussion scaffolds — who is this for? what does the writer/speaker assume? what is left unsaid? — support this shift.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Responding with cultural awareness is the intercultural dimension of the mediating strand. At Y7-8, engaging with this through a range of text types gives students a concrete, reusable analytical frame that deepens in EC05 and the Y9-10 descriptors.
success_criteria: Can identify at least one cultural reference or contextual feature in a target language text and explain its significance
Produces a response that is appropriate to the purpose and audience of the original text
